findings.english: The tubicolous polychaetes live in tubes, which they build or secrete and from which many of them never emerge. The fan worm Sabella builds a tube of mud and mucus and extends from the opening a crown of feathery tentacles, the radioles. The crown acts in two ways, for the capture of small food particles from the water, which are carried by cilia to the mouth, and for gas exchange, since it is richly supplied with blood. Serpula secretes a hard calcareous tube, which is fixed to rocks and shells, and the animal is able to close the opening by a plug, the operculum, formed from a modified tentacle.

findings.english: Excretion is by metanephridia, which occur as a pair in most segments. Each has a ciliated funnel, the nephrostome, which opens into the coelom of one segment, and a coiled tubule that passes through the septum behind it into the next segment and opens to the outside by a nephridiopore. Waste and some of the useful materials enter at the funnel, the useful materials are reabsorbed in the tubule, and urine is passed to the outside. The nephridia of earthworms are of several kinds, and they also help to regulate the water content of the body.

findings.english: The coelom is a large cavity that occupies the disc and extends into each arm, and it is filled with coelomic fluid that contains coelomocytes. It surrounds the gut and the gonads, and it extends into the papulae, where the fluid comes close to the sea water for gas exchange. The coelom is ciliated, and the beating of the cilia circulates the fluid. There is no excretory organ of the kind seen in an annelid, and the waste is taken by the coelomocytes, which migrate to the surface, particularly through the papulae, and are shed.

findings.english: Metamorphosis is the change from the bilateral larva to the pentaradial juvenile, and in the starfishes it takes place after the larva attaches. In the larva the left side of the coelom forms the rudiment of the water-vascular system as a five-lobed structure, and the rudiment grows on the left side of the body, while the right side forms less. The left side of the larva thus becomes the oral surface of the adult, and the right side the aboral surface, and the body is reorganised around the new axis. The larval arms and ciliary bands are absorbed, and the juvenile sets out its first tube feet.

findings.english: The characteristic feeding larva of many sea cucumbers is the auricularia. It is a transparent, bilaterally symmetrical larva with a single continuous ciliated band that runs in loops and lobes around the body, and it resembles the bipinnaria though it is not identical. The auricularia is followed in many species by a barrel-shaped larva with several separate rings of cilia, called the doliolaria, which does not feed, and which settles to the bottom and changes to a young sea cucumber.

findings.english: The sea urchins and brittle stars have a pluteus, which is a bilaterally symmetrical larva supported by long, slender, calcareous rods that hold out the arms. The ciliary band runs along the margins of the arms and the body, and the number and arrangement of the arms differ with the species and with the age of the larva. The pluteus of a sea urchin is called an echinopluteus, and that of a brittle star an ophiopluteus, and the two differ in the number of arms and in the pattern of the skeletal rods. The pluteus is very widely used in teaching of embryology and in laboratory work, because the eggs of sea urchins are easily fertilised and develop rapidly.

findings.english: The characteristic larva of many starfishes is the bipinnaria. It is a bilaterally symmetrical, transparent larva, a fraction of a millimetre to a few millimetres long, with looping ciliary bands that run on the surface, and a pair of lobed arm-like extensions of the body that are set in two groups. The band on the arms and body is used both in swimming and in the collection of unicellular algae, which are driven to the mouth. The gut is complete, with an oesophagus, a stomach and an intestine that opens at the anus.

findings.english: The early larvae of echinoderms differ in detail, but they can be compared to a hypothetical simple larva called the dipleurula, which is bilaterally symmetrical, ciliated, and has a band of cilia that runs in loops over the surface. The dipleurula is a model made by comparing living larvae, and it should not be described as an animal that has been seen. It is useful because it brings together the characters of the larvae of the echinoderms and of the hemichordates, in which the tornaria larva resembles the bipinnaria of the starfishes.

findings.english: A deuterostome is an animal in which, in typical development, the blastopore becomes the anus and the mouth forms secondarily, and in which the coelom forms from outgrowths of the gut. The echinoderms are deuterostomes on developmental grounds, and molecular studies support the placement. It is supported also by the larvae: bipinnaria in the starfishes, plutei in the sea urchins and brittle stars, and auricularia in the sea cucumbers. The larvae are bilateral, ciliated and free swimming, and resemble each other and the tornaria larva of the hemichordates.

findings.english: In Pila the foot is a broad, flat, muscular sole on which the animal creeps over the mud and plants of its pond. The sole is ciliated and rich in mucous glands, and locomotion is produced by waves of muscular contraction that pass along it. The waves are called pedal waves, and in a snail with a broad foot they may pass from the back to the front, so that parts of the sole are lifted and moved forward while the rest is attached. The mucus makes the movement smooth and also gives the grip needed to climb. The pace is slow, which is in keeping with the habit of grazing on algae and plant debris.

findings.english: The foot is a muscular outgrowth of the ventral body wall. It is made of interwoven muscle fibres running in several directions, with connective tissue and blood spaces between them, and it is supplied by a pair of pedal ganglia and the nerves from them. It is richly supplied with gland cells, which secrete mucus, and the surface carries cilia in many species. These features make it suited to creeping on a layer of mucus, which is the starting point for its other uses.

findings.english: The sexes are separate in most molluscs, though some gastropods are hermaphrodite. In marine forms the fertilised egg undergoes spiral cleavage and develops into a trochophore larva, which in most groups is followed by a veliger, with a shell and a ciliated velum used for swimming and feeding. Many freshwater and land forms have direct development, and some bivalves of fresh water, the unionids, have a special larva, the glochidium, which is a parasite on fish. The trochophore is one of the characters used to relate the molluscs to the annelids.

findings.english: The fertilised egg undergoes spiral cleavage and develops into a trochophore, a free-swimming larva with a band of cilia, the prototroch, around its middle and a tuft at the apex. It feeds on plankton. The trochophore elongates, acquires segments and chaetae, and becomes a metatrochophore and then a young worm that settles to the bottom, a stage in some species called the nectochaete. The trochophore is an important character linking the annelids with the molluscs, the larvae of which are similar.

findings.english: The nervous system consists of a bilobed brain in the prostomium, a pair of circumpharyngeal connectives and a double ventral nerve cord with a ganglion in each segment, from which nerves pass to the muscles and the parapodia. The eyes, palps, tentacles and cirri are the sense organs, and a pair of ciliated pits behind the prostomium, the nuchal organs, are chemoreceptors. The coelom is divided by septa, which in Nereis are thin, and the coelomic fluid serves as the hydrostatic skeleton.

findings.english: The circulation is closed. A dorsal vessel carries the blood forwards, a ventral vessel carries it backwards, and the two are joined in each segment by segmental vessels that supply the gut, the body wall and the parapodia. The blood contains a respiratory pigment dissolved in the plasma, and the dorsal vessel is contractile and drives the circulation. Excretion is by paired metanephridia in the segments, each opening into the coelom by a ciliated funnel and to the outside by a pore on the ventral side of the segment behind.

findings.english: The ciliated, solid, free-swimming larva of cnidarians.
findings.before: நிடேரியாக்களின் கசையிழை, திண்ம, சுதந்திரமாக நீந்தும் லார்வா.

findings.english: The zygote develops through a blastula into a ciliated, solid planula larva, which swims freely.
findings.before: கருமுட்டை பிளாஸ்டுலா வழியாக கசையிழை, திண்ம பிளானுலா லார்வாவாக வளர்ந்து சுதந்திரமாக நீந்துகிறது.

findings.english: The first adaptation is the covering of the body. A free-living flatworm has a ciliated epidermis. In flukes and tapeworms this is replaced by a tegument, which is a living syncytial layer that is continuous with cell bodies sunk into the parenchyma below. It is resistant to the digestive enzymes of the host. Its surface can be renewed, and in this way the parasite can alter the proteins on its surface, which assists in avoiding the immune response of the host.
findings.before: முதல் தகவமைப்பு உடலின் உறை. தனி வாழ்வுத் தட்டைப்புழுவுக்குக் கசையிழை எப்பிடெர்மிஸ் உண்டு. ஃப்ளூக்குகள், நாடாப்புழுக்களில் இது டெகுமென்ட்டால் மாற்றப்படுகிறது; அது கீழுள்ள பாரங்கைமாவில் மூழ்கிய செல் உடல்களுடன் தொடர்ச்சியான உயிருள்ள சின்சிட்டிய அடுக்கு. இது விருந்தோம்பியின் செரிமான நொதிகளை எதிர்க்கும். அதன் பரப்பு புதுப்பிக்கப்படலாம்; இவ்வாறு ஒட்டுண்ணி தன் பரப்பிலுள்ள புரதங்களை மாற்றி, விருந்தோம்பியின் நோயெதிர்ப்பு எதிர்வினையைத் தவிர்க்க உதவுகிறது.

findings.english: The planarian glides by the beating of the cilia of its ventral surface over a film of slime, and it wriggles by contraction of its muscles. The nervous system has a pair of anterior ganglia and two longitudinal nerve cords connected by cross-nerves, giving a ladder-like arrangement. The free-living flatworms are also famous for their power of regeneration, since a piece cut from a planarian may grow into a whole worm, a property that rests on the presence of undifferentiated cells scattered through the parenchyma.
findings.before: பிளனேரியன் வயிற்றுப் பரப்பின் கசையிழைகள் சளிப் படலத்தின் மேல் அசைவதால் வழுக்கிச் செல்கிறது; தசைச் சுருக்கத்தால் நெளிகிறது. நரம்பு மண்டலத்தில் ஒரு இணை முன்புற நரம்புத்திரள்களும், குறுக்கு நரம்புகளால் இணைந்த இரு நீளவாக்கு நரம்பு வடங்களும் உள்ளன; ஏணி போன்ற அமைப்பு. தனி வாழ்வுத் தட்டைப்புழுக்கள் மீளுருவாக்கத் திறனுக்கும் பிரபலமானவை; பிளனேரியனிலிருந்து வெட்டிய துண்டு முழுப் புழுவாக வளரலாம்; இத்திறன் பாரங்கைமா முழுவதும் சிதறிய வேறுபடாத செல்களைச் சார்ந்தது.

findings.english: Mostly free-living flatworms, found in fresh water, in the sea and in damp places on land. The body is covered with a ciliated epidermis, which contains rod-like bodies called rhabdites. The worm glides over surfaces on a film of mucus. The mouth is ventral and there is a muscular pharynx. Planaria is the common example, and its power of regeneration is well known.
findings.before: பெரும்பாலும் தனி வாழ்வுத் தட்டைப்புழுக்கள்; நன்னீர், கடல், நிலத்தின் ஈரமான இடங்களில் காணப்படுகின்றன. உடல் ராப்டைட்டுகள் எனப்படும் கோல் வடிவ உடலங்கள் கொண்ட கசையிழை எப்பிடெர்மிஸால் மூடப்பட்டுள்ளது. புழு சளிப் படலத்தின் மேல் பரப்புகளில் வழுக்கிச் செல்கிறது. வாய் வயிற்றுப் புறத்தில் உள்ளது; தசைத் தொண்டை உண்டு. பிளனேரியா பொதுவான எடுத்துக்காட்டு; அதன் மீளுருவாக்கத் திறன் நன்கு அறியப்பட்டது.

findings.english: A hollow excretory cell with a tuft of cilia that begins a protonephridial tubule.
findings.before: புரோட்டோநெஃப்ரிடியக் குழாயைத் தொடங்கும், கசையிழைக் கொத்துடைய வெற்று கழிவு நீக்க செல்.

findings.english: The excretory organs of flatworms are protonephridia. Each begins in a flame cell, a hollow cell in the parenchyma that has a tuft of beating cilia projecting into its cavity. The beating of the tuft resembles the flicker of a flame when seen under the microscope, and this is how the cell gets its name. The cilia draw fluid in through the fine slits of the wall of the cell and drive it into a capillary tubule. The tubules join to form larger ducts that open to the outside through one or more excretory pores.

findings.english: The ciliated swimming and feeding organ of the veliger larva.
findings.before: வெலிகர் லார்வாவின் கசையிழை நீந்தும், உண்ணும் உறுப்பு.
findings.after: வெலிகர் லார்வாவின் குறுஇழை நீந்தும், உண்ணும் உறுப்பு.

findings.english: A student should know that the consequences of torsion are fairly clear, but the reasons why it evolved are debated. The classical hypothesis, associated with Garstang, is that torsion benefited the larva, because when the larva was alarmed it could withdraw the head and the delicate ciliated swimming organ into the shell first, with the foot following as a plug, and so the head would be protected. A related adult benefit often given is that the head is withdrawn first and the strong foot or operculum closes the shell.
findings.before: முறுக்கலின் விளைவுகள் ஓரளவு தெளிவு; ஆனால் அது ஏன் பரிணமித்தது என்பது விவாதிக்கப்படுகிறது என மாணவர் அறிய வேண்டும். கார்ஸ்டாங்குடன் தொடர்புடைய செம்மையான கருதுகோள்: முறுக்கல் லார்வாவுக்கு நன்மை தந்தது; ஏனெனில் லார்வா அச்சமடையும்போது தலையையும் மென்மையான கசையிழை நீந்தும் உறுப்பையும் முதலில் ஓட்டுக்குள் இழுக்க, பாதம் அடைப்பானாகத் தொடர, தலை பாதுகாக்கப்படும். தொடர்புடைய, அடிக்கடி தரப்படும் முதிர்ந்த நன்மை, தலை முதலில் இழுக்கப்பட்டு வலிமையான பாதம் அல்லது ஆப்பர்குலம் ஓட்டை மூடுவது.

findings.english: Each tube foot is a hollow, extensible cylinder with a flattened disc at the tip, and the base of the foot is connected through the skeleton to a muscular bulb, the ampulla, which lies in the coelom. The wall of the foot has longitudinal muscle fibres and connective tissue, and the lining is ciliated. The foot works as a piston. When the ampulla contracts, the valve in the lateral canal closes, so that the fluid is forced into the foot and not back into the radial canal. The fluid pressure extends the foot.
findings.before: ஒவ்வொரு குழாய்ப்பாதமும் முனையில் தட்டையான வட்டுடைய வெற்று, நீளக்கூடிய உருளை; பாதத்தின் அடி கூடு வழியே உடற்குழியிலுள்ள தசைக் குமிழான ஆம்புலாவுடன் இணைந்துள்ளது. பாதத்தின் சுவரில் நீள்தசை இழைகளும் இணைப்புத் திசுவும் உள்ளன; உட்புறம் கசையிழை கொண்டது. பாதம் உலக்கையாகச் செயல்படுகிறது. ஆம்புலா சுருங்கும்போது பக்கக் கால்வாயின் வால்வு மூடுகிறது; எனவே திரவம் கதிர்க் கால்வாய்க்குப் பின்னோக்கி அல்லாமல் பாதத்துக்குள் தள்ளப்படுகிறது. திரவ அழுத்தம் பாதத்தை நீட்டுகிறது.
